description: The primary portal is bot-defended and its award data is not search-indexed, so no reliable read path has been proven yet.
The machine-readable ESJN concluded-contracts dataset on data.gov.mk has not been located, downloaded or schema-checked.
No local-language keyword/CPV filter set exists for banking and payments IT subjects.

Beyond NBRSM, the set of relevant contracting authorities for payments/banking IT (Управа за јавни приходи, Царинска управа, Фонд за ПИОМ, ЗФРМ, state-owned enterprises, municipalities operating payment services) has not been enumerated.
Unknown how far back the portal's public archive and any bulk dataset reach, and whether pre-2019 (old ZJN) records are retained.
Award notices name winners; the competitor set (losing bidders) is only partially visible, mainly via appeals decisions and evaluation reports.
Procurements below the mandatory e-publication threshold, and central-bank procurements potentially exempt or confidential, will not appear in the ESJN.
TED's own faceted search and bulk/open-data endpoints were not exercised, so the actual volume and CPV distribution of MK financial-infrastructure notices is unknown.

ECEPP was not queried for the North Macedonia + financial institutions filter, so it is unknown how many live and historic MK financial-sector notices it holds or whether award notices are publicly readable without login.

The National Bank of North Macedonia (Народна банка на Република Северна Македонија) appears as a donor counterpart (WBG electronic-payments assessment) but its own procurement/tender pages were not located in this run.

Other IFIs plausibly active in MK financial infrastructure were not searched: CEB (Council of Europe Development Bank), IFC advisory, EFSE/Finance in Motion, GGF, and the EU's WB Guarantee/Growth Plan Reform and Growth Facility.
Macedonian-language coverage relied on Cyrillic terms only; Albanian-language and Latin-script Macedonian variants were not searched, and MK institutions increasingly publish Albanian versions.
No historical baseline was established: it is unknown which international vendors have previously won donor-funded MK financial-infrastructure contracts.
Regional/multi-country lots (Western Balkans, EU4Digital) hide MK relevance inside eligibility text, so country-field filtering will miss them.
MK job ads are ephemeral — banks and boards delete ads after the application deadline and there is no national archive of vacancy text.

Career pages resolved for only a minority of MK banks (Stopanska, NLB, Komercijalna root) and vendors; the rest of the ~13-bank market plus vendors (Duna, Seavus, Semos, Sorsix, Netcetera, Edusoft) are unmapped for hiring signals.
CV-side coverage is thin and legally constrained — LinkedIn is gated, and no MK-specific public CV repository was identified.
Albanian-language hiring channels were not searched, despite a substantial Albanian-speaking workforce and banks (e.g. TTK, Halkbank) recruiting in it.
No structured-data access path (API, RSS, JSON endpoint) was confirmed for any MK job board in this pass.
Coverage is Skopje-centric; branch and regional IT/operations ads (Štip, Bitola, Tetovo, Strumica) were only incidentally observed.

Speaker, agenda and sponsor pages of the regional events (infintech.me/speakers, money-motion.eu sponsors, paybalkan sponsor page) were identified but not individually fetched and parsed for MK affiliations.
Albanian-language MK sources were out of the run's language scope (mk, en) despite a large Albanian-speaking MK business community and Tirana-hosted regional payments events.

Trade expos/fairs (e.g. Skopje Fair / Скопски саем technology or finance editions), university-hosted ICT conferences (ICT Innovations), and startup/venture events with fintech tracks were not searched.
No archived-editions strategy was established; most event sites overwrite sponsor walls each year, destroying the year-over-year signal this cell depends on.
Only two vendor newsrooms (ASEE/Payten, Natech) were captured as examples of the vendor-side sponsorship-disclosure pattern.
The State Treasury (Трезор) within the Ministry of Finance and its payment/settlement operations were not separately located; no treasury-specific portal or document store was identified.
Sub-national public buyers (municipalities, City of Skopje) and state-owned enterprises that procure POS/payment and fiscalisation technology were not covered in this cell pass.

Audit and oversight bodies — Државен завод за ревизија (State Audit Office) and Државна комисија за жалби по јавни набавки (procurement appeals commission) — were not searched; both publish findings that reveal how state payment/IT contracts were awarded and contested.
Albanian-language (sq) government publications were out of the declared run scope (mk, en) but a substantial share of official communication and business media in North Macedonia is bilingual.

EU accession instruments — IPA programming documents, the annual EC Country Report chapters on taxation and financial services, and the Secretariat for European Affairs (СЕП) — were not covered, though they fund and schedule much of the payments/digitalisation programme.
КЗК and ДКЖЈН decision corpora were reachable only at navigation level; individual decisions were not retrievable through search.
Службен весник на РСМ (Official Gazette) was not scouted as a source in this pass, yet it is where licence withdrawals, sanctions and supervisory decisions become legally public.
Administrative Court (Управен суд) and Misdemeanour court decisions on appeals against КЗК/НБРСМ/АЗЛП actions were not directly scouted (only the КЗК's own court-decisions page).

North Macedonia is officially bilingual (mk/sq) and institutions such as ДЗР brand themselves as 'Enti Shtetëror i Revizionit', but the run's language scope is mk+en only, so Albanian-language enforcement/audit publications were not searched.

Internal audit / public internal financial control (Централна единица за хармонизација, Министерство за финансии PFM monitoring) reports were only glimpsed via a Ministry of Finance PFM monitoring document and not scouted as a standing source.
e-nabavki.gov.mk is an ASP.NET application whose data sits behind .aspx grids and .asmx services; no confirmed bulk-export or open-data endpoint was identified.
No company-registry source was captured (Central Registry of RNM) to resolve ownership, founding dates and shareholders of MK payment startups.
App-store listings (Google Play / App Store MK) for wallets and payment apps were not enumerated; they carry release cadence, changelogs and SDK/partner hints.
Individual remittance operator MK pages (Western Union, Ria, MoneyGram, Intel Express, Zolotaya Korona-type corridors) were not individually enumerated.
Albanian-language sources were not searched, although Albanian is widely used in MK and some payment/remittance actors communicate in it.
No developer/API documentation portal for MK gateways was directly captured (cPay technical docs, bank e-commerce developer pages).

The archive lane (Wayback CDX enumeration of MK bank domains kb.com.mk, stb.com.mk, nlb.mk, halkbank.mk, sparkasse.mk, ttk.com.mk, uni.com.mk and vendor domains printec.com, see.asseco.com, nextsense.com, duna.mk, seavus.com) was defined but not executed.

The richest structured aggregators for this cell (SeeNews full archive, EMIS company profiles, bne IntelliNews, AppsRunTheWorld customer database) are subscription-gated, so only headlines and teasers were observable.

Rating agencies and commercial market-research houses covering MK banking (Fitch/Moody's/S&P country and bank reports, RBI CEE Banking Sector Report, EY/PwC/Deloitte SEE banking studies) were not searched in this run.
No URL in this slice was liveness-verified; several are recorded from search-result listings only, and blocked flags are inferences from listing behaviour rather than confirmed HTTP responses.

Macedonian-language coverage in this cell is thin by nature: regional/international aggregators publish about MK in English, and only the EC report translation portal supplied substantive MK-language material.

Register contents themselves were never read — only their page URLs and descriptions were confirmed, because of the domain-wide 403. The actual list of licensed PIs, EMIs and payment-system operators remains uncollected.
The exemption/limited-network register and any register of account-information/payment-initiation service providers (AIS/PIS under the PSD2-aligned law) were not located as distinct pages.
No confirmed machine-readable endpoint for the registers; NBStat API is referenced in NBRSM terms-of-use text but its base URL and whether it covers payments tables were not verified.
No historical/archival capture strategy: registers are live pages that are overwritten, so licence grants and revocations leave no visible trail.

Register entries were not cross-linked to the Central Registry of RNM (Централен регистар) company data or to Official Gazette (Службен весник) publications of licensing decisions — outside this cell but essential for entity resolution and ownership.
Halkbank, ProCredit, UNIBanka and Centralna kooperativna banka are covered only at root-domain or reports-page level; their press-release archives are not yet located.
Bank IT job advertisements — which name concrete platforms (core, card management, AML, ESB) — were not searched at all this pass.

Only one vendor mirror (Asseco SEE) was explored. Other likely suppliers to MK banks (card personalisation, ATM/POS, digital onboarding, PKI) have their own case-study libraries that were not searched.
No historical back-fill depth was assessed beyond noting NLB's 2016-2026 year filters; the archive depth of Komercijalna, Stopanska and the smaller banks is unknown.

English-language subsidiary reporting by foreign parents (NLB Group, Erste/Steiermärkische, ProCredit Holding, Halkbank TR, CCB Sofia, OTP for Stopanska) was not systematically collected; group reports often describe MK-subsidiary IT programmes in more detail than the local site.
SEINet's technical access characteristics (JS gating, session requirements, bulk export) were not tested, despite it being the single highest-leverage pointer in the cell.
The entire nbrm.mk cluster (operator register, MIPS/KIBS/CaSys system pages, payment statistics, ZPUPS PDF) is unverified because of 403 bot defence.

Bank-side acquiring/issuing units (Komercijalna banka, Stopanska banka, NLB, Halkbank, Sparkasse card centres) were not individually scouted in this pass — they are the counterparties of the switch and the buyers of terminal tech.

No tender/procurement source was covered (e.g. the national public procurement bureau e-nabavki, or KIBS/NBRNM RFPs for the MIPS replacement programme), yet the EU-supported MIPS modernisation is live and is the largest infrastructure vendor opportunity in the cell.
No developer/integration documentation (API specs, ISO 20022 message guides, 3-D Secure/tokenisation onboarding docs) was located for KIBS Instant or the CaSys e-commerce gateway.

Recruitment ads for CaSys and KIBS (seen referenced on bankarstvo.mk) were not systematically collected, although job postings are one of the few sources that name concrete platform/vendor technologies in use.

Only a handful of MK banks (Komercijalna, Stopanska, Halkbank) produced any vendor-side evidence. NLB Banka Skopje, Sparkasse Bank Makedonija, ProCredit, Silk Road Bank, TTK Banka, Centralna Kooperativna Banka, UNIBanka, Capital Bank and the Development Bank of North Macedonia are entirely uncovered on the vendor-reference axis.

AML/compliance, fraud, card-issuance/personalisation (IDEMIA, G+D, Thales), HSM/security, instant-payments and clearing infrastructure vendors were only touched indirectly; no dedicated sweep was done for MK-named references in these segments.

Public-procurement and tender records (e-nabavki.gov.mk) and state-owned/Development Bank IT tenders were not searched, although these publish awarded supplier names and contract values — often the only hard confirmation of a vendor-bank relationship.

Albanian-language sources were not searched at all, despite a large Albanian-speaking market segment in MK and vendors (e.g. CaSys' Albanian fintech partner Rubicon) operating across the MK-AL corridor.
Findings cluster on recent (2023-2026) digital-channel launches; older core-banking and card-platform selections that still define incumbency were not traced.

No evidence found for the ATM / self-service / POS hardware reseller and maintenance channel in North Macedonia — who distributes and services NCR, Diebold Nixdorf, Wincor, and cash-handling equipment for MK banks.

Only one vendor partner directory (Thales CPL) was actually reached. Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, Cisco, Entrust, Temenos, Salesforce, UiPath and Diebold partner locators were not queried for North Macedonia, yet these are the definitive source of partner STATUS and tier for local integrators.

Macedonian search worked well for actor discovery (банкарски софтвер, електронско банкарство, референци) but produced almost nothing for partner-status vocabulary — овластен партнер, сертифициран партнер, златен партнер, дистрибутер, имплементациски партнер were not systematically exercised.

This cell approached the vendor→bank link only from the integrator side. Bank-side artefacts that name suppliers — annual reports, e-banking terms & conditions, mobile app privacy policies, TLS certificate and DNS records of banking portals — were not examined.

Newly discovered or partially discovered actors — Melon Solutions, Ultra, Ентаер лоџик ДИТ, БЦС, Accent, SoftNET, Aitroniks, Sorsix, IT Labs, Interworks, Akton, Login Systems, Revoit — have no confirmed finance references yet.
Several of the strongest artefacts found are point-in-time (a 2020 INREKOM e-banking study, individual news items). No continuous feed was established for vendor–bank announcements.
The concrete public search endpoint(s) of the Central Registry (free basic-profile lookup and any ЕМБС query URL) were not pinned down in this run.

The seed queries referenced NKD codes 6499 and 6612, but no source was found that lets one browse MK entities by activity code for free; the mapping from payments/banking-software business models to NKD Rev.2/2.1 codes (62.01, 62.09, 63.11, 64.99, 66.19, 66.12) has not been validated against MK usage.

Registry-adjacent event sources were not covered in this run: insolvency/liquidation announcements, pledge and leasing registers, and Службен весник publication of registry-related acts — all of which reveal vendor distress, secured financing and corporate restructuring.

Fees, licensing terms and permitted reuse for CRM's Distribution System and for CompanyWall's Web API were not read from primary terms documents; the MKD 5,000 figure comes from a search snippet only.
Business registries are structurally poor for the 'case studies' topic — they record existence and finances, not deployments or references. This cell produced almost nothing on that topic.
Professional/certification bodies adjacent to banking (internal auditors, compliance officers, information-security associations such as an MK ISACA chapter) were not searched in this pass.
No Albanian-language searching was performed, per run scope (mk, en only).
Association member lists are HTML-only; no API, CSV or open-data export was found for MASIT, MBA or mchamber.mk.
Association archives (past assemblies, historical member rosters, older bulletins) were not enumerated; only current pages were sighted.
Association event calendars, sponsor and exhibitor lists (MASIT forums, MBA conferences, Macedonian Stock Exchange annual conference) were only sampled, not systematically catalogued.
No MK-language marketing/PR trade outlet (e.g. Marketing365-type media) or specialised procurement-watch portal was confirmed, so vendor-side campaign and tender announcements in MK are uncovered.

Historical archives (pre-2015 deal announcements, executive moves, outage reports) were not probed; TIME.mk's own note indicates its full archive search covers 2000-2012, a different window from live monitoring.
Albanian-language coverage is represented (Portalb, Zhurnal, Aktuale, Telegrafi) but Turkish-language MK media, relevant given Halkbank's Turkish ownership, was not searched at all.
System outage and incident reporting — an explicit rationale for this cell — was not evidenced by any retrieved article; only launches and policy items surfaced.
